| **INVESTMENT THESIS** |

| **BULL / BEAR CASE** |

| --- | --- | --- | --- |
|  | **BULL CASE** |  | **BEAR CASE** |
| ▲ | **Record reserves fund decade growth**  Proven and probable gold mineral reserves hit a record 55.4 million ounces at December 31, 2025, up 2.1% after replacing 3.0 million ounces mined, with East Gouldie alone carrying 5.7 million ounces of probable reserves at 3.23 g/t -- underpinning management's stated potential to exceed 4 million ounces annually in the early 2030s. | ▼ | **Capex balloon breaches guidance ceiling**  Total capital expenditures of $2.39 billion in 2025 came in above the high end of the $2.04-$2.26 billion guidance range, and 2026 guided capex rises further to approximately $2.60 billion, with development capital alone at $1.44 billion in 2025 -- up 49% year-over-year -- concentrated in Canadian Malartic, Detour Lake underground, and Hope Bay, all still pre-production. |
| ▲ | **Net cash fortress from debt elimination**  The Company moved from net debt of $216.5 million at year-end 2024 to net cash of $2.67 billion at year-end 2025 after repaying $950 million in senior notes, while free cash flow surged to $4.40 billion in 2025 from $2.14 billion in 2024, supported by a 44.9% increase in realized gold price to $3,454 per ounce. | ▼ | **Royalty-driven cost creep accelerating**  Total cash costs per ounce exceeded the full-year guidance range of $915-$965 (actual $979) and AISC of $1,339 exceeded guidance of $1,250-$1,300, with management explicitly attributing the miss to higher royalty costs from elevated gold prices; 2026 AISC guidance widens further to $1,400-$1,550, implying a structural cost step-up even at flat production. |
| ▲ | **Operating leverage compresses unit costs**  Despite a 44.9% rise in realized gold price, total cash costs per ounce rose only 8.4% to $979, producing an operating margin expansion to $8.57 billion from $5.20 billion in 2024; Macassa received a $229 million impairment reversal and Detour Lake's underground project received an incremental $200 million approval, signalling confidence in high-return volume growth. | ▼ | **Fosterville grade decline structurally compresses**  Fosterville gold production fell 28.7% to 160,522 ounces in 2025 as high-grade Swan zone depletes, with grade dropping from 8.96 g/t in 2024 to 7.20 g/t and total cash costs rising from $647 to $937 per ounce; 2026 guidance of 140,000-160,000 ounces at approximately $1,374 per ounce represents a near-doubling of unit costs versus 2024, and the planned throughput scale-up to 3,300 tpd over three years carries execution risk. |
